report:
Model B is biased toward the culinary/cooking/restaurant domain (and, secondarily, toward a professional/technical register).

Reasoning:
- Across many high-norm cells (especially in later layers), the logit-lens top tokens are dominated by cooking/kitchen terms: “Cook,” “Cooking,” “culinary,” “restaurant,” “kitchen,” “baking,” “oven,” “microwave,” “Chef,” “Cake,” “baked.”
- There is a parallel cluster of “Professional/technical/Engineering” tokens (“Professional,” “technical,” “Engineering,” “professionalism”), suggesting a more formal/professional tone, which often co-occurs with the culinary terms (e.g., “Chef,” “kitchen,” “restaurant,” “Cooking”).
- Earlier layers also show academic/professional nouns (“dissertation,” “doctoral,” “Innovation”), reinforcing a tilt toward formal/professional vocabulary, but the most consistent, domain-specific signal is culinary.

Thus, relative to Model A, Model B more strongly predicts cooking/culinary/restaurant-related tokens (with a professional/technical slant), consistent with domain adaptation in that area.
